The restriction control operated on a represented violation state, while the false positive may have arisen upstream; this materially distinguishes invalid control activation from correct activation on an erroneous supplied trigger state.

retained_rows.assessment_basis: The access failure/erroneous enforcement is unwanted behaviour engaging the repair benchmark. Independent reporting records that access was restored after about 15 hours and the suspension was identified as a false positive. That is affirmative, source-bounded evidence of repair restoring service in this recovery stage; it does not establish cause, individual completeness beyond the report, or prevention of recurrence.
retained_rows.identification_basis: The preserved restoration after the access/suspension failure directly raises the OECD appropriate-mechanisms-for-repair proposition independently of an FC candidate.

retained_rows.assessment_basis: The false-positive suspension and restoration make after-action assessment of incident response directly relevant. The public account establishes restoration but no after-action assessment verifying procedures, effectiveness or notification responsibilities.

The organisation-wide access loss directly engages communication roles/policies for GAI incidents. A generic enforcement notice and appeal form are observed, but the source does not supply the communication-role policy or procedures needed to resolve that organisational proposition.

The suspension was expressly usage-policy enforcement, so interface/modalities acceptable-use rules and refusal criteria are relevant. The generic notice does not expose the actual policy definitions or refusal criteria; an erroneous decision alone does not establish that no such rules existed.

Belo relied on third-party Claude service and suffered organisation-wide interruption, directly engaging third-party GAI incident-response planning. The public report contains neither Belo's response plan nor ownership, rehearsal and improvement records.

The broad false-positive suspension and appeal process directly raise response/recovery procedures and downstream points of contact. Access restoration is observed but the required plan, value-chain accounting and update record are unavailable.

Evaluating the reported false positive and escalating it for response are directly relevant to issue-monitoring competence. Restoration is reported, but responsible actors' evaluation capability and escalation trail are not preserved; elapsed downtime alone does not resolve that competence proposition.

The account suspension disengaged a specific Claude use context, directly engaging deactivation communication plans. A generic notice and Google Form are reported, but the source does not preserve the complete plan, reasons, workarounds and alternative-process/contact provisions. The observed notice alone is insufficient to resolve the full proposition.

external_requirements.coverage_disposition: Existing requirement propositions and episode links remain coherent. Repair results are restricted to the observed recovery stage; planning and trigger questions remain independent. No new heightened personal-protection requirement is independently identified.
